clue.text: One can't see the bird for, the feathers in this

definitions.text: One can't see the bird for, the feathers in this

parts.words: One can't see the bird for, the feathers in this
parts.note: a bird here is a young woman, a stage performer hidden behind big feathered fans as she dances

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher complains that plumage blocks the view of the bird itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is old slang for a young woman, and the feathers are the fans a burlesque dancer hides behind, so nobody sees the 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque routine where the performer is screened by large ostrich-plume fans is known by this name.

clue.text: What old soldiers. without Bill at the front

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: the song says old soldiers never die, they only fade away
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Old soldiers carry on at the front line with no Bill among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old soldiers never die, they simply fade away' is the song. 'without' means outside here, so FADE goes around AC.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's face, its main outward-facing wall, is the front.

clue.text: He describes Lady Clara Vere de .Vere's. blood

definitions.text: He describes Lady Clara Vere de .Vere's. blood

parts.words: He describes Lady Clara Vere de .Vere's. blood
parts.note: Tennyson's poem Lady Clara Vere de Vere says simple faith is more than this blood, the aristocratic ancestry of the Conqueror's invaders

explanation.surface: A poet is pictured writing about a noblewoman's ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem ends 'Kind hearts are more than coronets, And simple faith than ___ blood'; the word filling the gap also names a man, the 'He'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for descendants of William the Conqueror's invaders, and also a man's first name.

clue.text: Publicity stunt that makes : exciting reading

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, publicity
a stunt is a daring undertaking, a venture

explanation.surface: A promotional gimmick generates thrilling press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling tale of daring escapades is a genre of story that grips readers.

clue.text: Perfection Hamlet so devoutly wished

definitions.meaning: completion or fulfilment, the ultimate end
in the 'to be or not to be' speech Hamlet calls death a thing devoutly to be wished

explanation.surface: Hamlet longed earnestly for things to be flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fulfilment or completion, and Hamlet's soliloquy calls death this, devoutly to be wished.

clue.text: Whereby one reckons to get a hundred in a vehicle

indicators.note: in places the hundred inside the vehicle phrase, cutting it open

parts.note: a, plus bus, a vehicle
a, plus C, the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A bus driver hopes to rack up a hundred passengers on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AC (a hundred) inside A BUS, between the B and the U.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires is the old device used to count and do sums.

clue.text: Pooh had about a pound, being dim:

indicators.note: had about says the bear holds the pound within it, wrapped around

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is a bear
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A slow-witted teddy bear is found with a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pooh' is A. A. Milne's bear of little brain, which also fits 'dim' in the surface. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary, misty or blurred, as eyes are when tired, is the old adjective's sense.

clue.text: Many like a new bright star, the Great Lover

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a lot of anything
as means like, in the manner of
a nova is a star that suddenly flares up bright, newly visible

explanation.surface: A celebrity is acclaimed as the dazzling new heart-throb.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova was an 18th-century Venetian adventurer famous for his seductions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian adventurer whose memoirs recount countless seductions is the byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Separated some rocks under Edinburgh

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of the rock beneath Edinburgh has split apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the S of 'rocks' and ends at the ED of 'Edinburgh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Split apart or torn asunder is the old literary sense of the verb.

clue.text: Rolling home" might describe one of them'

definitions.text: Rolling home" might describe one of them'

parts.words: Rolling home" might describe one of them'
parts.note: the song phrase about heading happily home is read literally: a home on wheels that rolls along the road

explanation.surface: A sailors' song title is applied to some unnamed group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Home' sounds like a homeward song, but read literally it is a dwelling that rolls on wheels behind a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Trailers towed by cars and used as mobile dwellings are rolling homes in the literal sense.

clue.text: He is the third

parts.note: in grammar the pronoun he belongs to the third of the grammatical categories, after I and you

explanation.surface: Someone is named as third in a line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man in a queue, but grammar calls he, she and it the third of these categories.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar ranks pronouns as first, second and third; he is third-category, so the grammarian's term completes the phrase.

clue.text: The normally prescribed means of illumination ?

definitions.text: The normally prescribed means of illumination ?

parts.words: The normally prescribed means of illumination ?
parts.note: the regulation or standard-issue way of lighting a room, read as a tall household light on a pole

explanation.surface: A question about the officially approved way to light something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Normally prescribed' sounds like a regulation, but it is the adjective for the tall floor lamp on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall floor-standing lamp with a shade is named as if it were the regulation light.

clue.text: 500 pennies from heaven go down it

definitions.text: 500 pennies from heaven go down it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the song title's pennies from heaven are falling rain

explanation.surface: A windfall of coins tumbles out of the sky and disappears into a gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Money wasted is said to go 'down the drain', and rain, the heavenly pennies, also flows down one, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainwater runs into a gutter outlet, and squandered cash proverbially vanishes the same way.

clue.text: What's said of nature etc for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the two words are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A remark about nature and other such topics, offered for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' shuffles NATURE and ETC into the answer; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything spoken aloud, a remark or statement, is a synonym for what has been said.

clue.text: Leg trap perhaps to show general superiority in the field ?

definitions.meaning: a leg trap is a cricket field placing of close fielders set to get the batsman out, a ploy for a dismissal

definitions.text: to show general superiority in the field
definitions.meaning: to beat an opponent by cleverer moves, as a general would on the battlefield

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's close-field trap proves who rules the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg trap is a ring of close fielders on the leg side set to catch the batsman out; read as two words the answer is a plan for a dismissal. 'General' is also the army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a scheme aimed at a dismissal in cricket and the verb for beating a rival by superior tactics.

clue.text: His fist should be ready to resist" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: His fist should be ready to resist" (Gilbert)

parts.words: His fist should be ready to resist" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a gap-fill from the HMS Pinafore song about the British tar, whose vigorous fist resists a dictatorial word

explanation.surface: A line of comic-opera verse about a sailor's readiness to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: In HMS Pinafore the song 'A British tar' says 'His ___ fist should be ready to resist a dictatorial word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert's line describes the tar's fist as vigorous and forceful, which is what the missing adjective means.

clue.text: Blackleg promises to pay for the bloomer

parts.note: a blackleg is a strike-breaker, a scab
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A strike-breaker pledges to pay for someone's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a flowering plant: a thing that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant with pincushion-like blue heads is a meadow flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: A worker among the non-, married-because he's this?

indicators.note: among places the worker within the unmarried word

parts.note: unwed means not married
the worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is still single, and someone guesses the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts ANT inside UNWED. The definition invites a cruel guess why he has stayed single: no one desired him.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor who stayed single may be so because no one desired him, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Thought very hard of prisoners in a camp

definitions.meaning: gathered together in one place, as inmates in a wartime internment camp are

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war broods intensely about his captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both applied the mind fiercely and herded together, as in the wartime camps named after this gathering.

clue.text: Irishman, takes part when e's off police duty

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name, short for Patrick

indicators.note: off says the letter is taken away from the part word

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
the letter e

explanation.surface: An Irish constable takes on a job when he is off duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops the E from ROLE to leave ROL; 'takes' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat walked by constables or soldiers to keep watch is a round of police work.

clue.text: Remained sober, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is a word that sounds like the clue word's synonym

parts.note: staid means sober, sedate

explanation.surface: Someone stayed off the drink, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stopped on in a place rather than leave is a synonym for remained.

clue.text: Author, of. Cimmerian Trees?.

parts.note: Cimmerian means intensely dark, from the mythical land of perpetual night
a wood is a stand of trees

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote of dark forests in a mythical land.
explanation.walkthrough: Algernon Blackwood was an English writer of ghost and supernatural stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Blackwood was an English writer of supernatural tales, so he is a writer of books.

clue.text: What a lark to destroy a native village !

indicators.note: to destroy says the letters are broken up and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims how amusing it would be to wreck a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a lark' looks like an exclamation of fun; 'a lark' is the fodder. A kraal is a southern African village of huts within a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern African settlement of huts enclosed by a fence is this Afrikaans word.

clue.text: Admit the general

definitions.meaning: concede or allow that something is true
Ulysses S. ..., Union commander in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let the commanding officer in.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede a point, and the surname of the Union army's leading commander, later US president.

clue.text: Disbursement : is' not in lyrical work

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a lay is a short narrative or lyric poem

explanation.surface: An accountant says some payment is missing from a book of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid out, an expenditure, is what this word describes.

clue.text: Try meals cooked a la maitre?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of the two words are prepared afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A diner is urged to sample dishes prepared in the style of a master chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TRY and MEALS. 'A la maitre' is French for 'in the manner of a master', which defines the adjective, and maitre also suggests the head chef of the kitchen surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the style of an expert or master craftsman, hence highly skilled.

clue.text: One's up in this.

parts.note: a rider is said to be up when mounted on the horse, sitting on this leather seat

explanation.surface: Someone is awake and busy with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like out of bed, but a jockey who is 'up' is mounted, sitting on the horse's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat strapped on a horse is where a mounted rider sits.

clue.text: Like Dr. Roylott's murderous' band

parts.note: in a Sherlock Holmes story Dr Grimesby Roylott kills with a snake whose markings form a spotted band

explanation.surface: A villain's deadly gang is compared to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a gang of thugs, but in Conan Doyle's story it is the dotted marking on a deadly swamp adder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conan Doyle story title names the band as dotted with spots, which is what the adjective means.
